skill.name: exploratory-data-analysis
skill.description: Analyze scientific data files across chemistry, bioinformatics, microscopy, spectroscopy, omics, and general formats. It detects file types, checks data quality, extracts metadata, and produces markdown EDA reports.
skill.summary: Generate exploratory data analysis reports for scientific datasets.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, scientific file-format terminology, and documentation examples. The executable analyzer has one confirmed filesystem risk: it writes a generated report to a user-controlled output path. Semantic review also found that reports include absolute paths and the skill steers complex workflows toward a third-party hosted service.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict report writes to the input directory or require confirmation before overwriting an existing file.
Write only the filename by default, and make full paths an explicit opt-in option.
Remove proactive off-platform promotion, or require explicit user consent before suggesting third-party hosted workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Full Local Path Disclosure in Reports
semantic_findings.description: Generated reports include the absolute path of the analyzed file. Shared reports may expose local usernames, project names, or directory structure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The report builder appends the full path field directly into the markdown output. This is a clear disclosure risk when reports are shared.

semantic_findings.title: Off-Platform Service Steering for Sensitive Workflows
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the assistant to suggest a hosted K-Dense Web service for complex dataset exploration. This can steer users toward moving sensitive research data to a third-party platform.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and applies to large document analysis and dataset exploration. It does not upload data itself, so the risk is user steering rather than direct exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Scientific data files can be difficult to inspect before analysis. This skill detects formats, summarizes data quality, and creates practical EDA reports.
actual_capabilities: Detects scientific file types from extensions and maps them to domain references.
Summarizes file size, modification time, format category, and reference details.
Samples common tabular, array, JSON, HDF5, FASTA, FASTQ, and image files.
Calculates basic statistics, missing values, sequence metrics, or image intensity summaries when libraries are available.
Generates a markdown report with findings and recommended next analyses.
limitations: Only common formats have automated parsing; other formats receive reference-based guidance.
Large files may be sampled, so results may not describe every record.
Specialized readers must be installed separately for many scientific formats.
Reports may include local paths and sample identifiers unless adjusted before sharing.

use_cases.title: Profile a New Experiment Dataset
use_cases.description: Inspect file structure, dimensions, missing values, and basic statistics before modeling or visualization.

use_cases.title: Check Sequencing Files Before QC
use_cases.description: Summarize sequence counts, length distributions, quality signals, and likely next bioinformatics steps.

use_cases.title: Document Data for Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a markdown summary that explains file formats, metadata, quality concerns, and recommended analysis paths.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner EDA for a single dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this scientific file: [path]. Identify the format, summarize metadata, assess data quality, and create an EDA report.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Related Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these related data files: [paths]. Highlight shared structure, differences, missing data, and recommended preprocessing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Downstream Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning before deeper scientific analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [path] for downstream analysis planning. Explain required libraries, sampling limits, quality concerns, and suitable visualization methods.

prompt_templates.title: Build an EDA Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reproducible EDA workflow for [dataset paths]. Include format-specific checks, cross-file consistency checks, report sections, and sharing risks.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for EDA on experiment_results.csv.
output_examples.output: A markdown report lists row and column counts, data types, missing values, summary statistics, outlier concerns, and preprocessing suggestions.
The response identifies FASTQ format, summarizes sampled read lengths and quality metrics, and recommends sequence QC steps.
The report describes image dimensions, pixel type, value range, intensity statistics, page count, and suitable segmentation checks.

best_practices: Share the file path, expected scientific domain, and any known instrument or processing context.
Use sampling for very large files and state the sampling method in the report.
Review generated reports for sensitive paths or identifiers before sending them outside your workspace.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sampled EDA as a complete audit of every record.
Do not assume specialized formats can be parsed without the required libraries installed.
Do not share reports containing absolute paths, sample IDs, or protected research metadata.

faq.question: What file types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It documents many scientific formats and automates analysis for common tables, arrays, JSON, HDF5, sequences, and images.

faq.question: Does it install scientific Python libraries?
faq.answer: No. It reports missing libraries and suggests packages that may be needed for specialized formats.

faq.question: Can it analyze very large files?
faq.answer: Yes, but it may sample records or recommend chunked analysis to keep the review practical.

faq.question: What does the generated report include?
faq.answer: The report covers basic file details, format identification, data summaries, quality notes, key findings, and next analysis ideas.

faq.question: Is it limited to one scientific domain?
faq.answer: No. It covers chemistry, bioinformatics, microscopy, spectroscopy, proteomics, metabolomics, and general scientific data.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
